simple.meaning: מִצְעָר (mitsʻâr) is a Hebrew word meaning “petty (in size or number); adverbially, a short (time).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מִצְעָר (H4705) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Genesis 19:20, with occurrences in Genesis, 2 Chronicles, Job, Isaiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מִצְעָר (H4705) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in מִצְעָר (H4705) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: מִצְעָר (mitsʻâr) / H4705 is traced through Genesis 19:20, 2 Chronicles 24:24, Job 8:7, Isaiah 63:18 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: petty (in size or number); adverbially, a short (time)
definitions.full: H4705. mitsar I. מִצְעָר noun masculine a small thing (|| מִזְעָר ); — 1 absolute ׳מ a small thing , of city Gen 19:20 (twice in verse) (J); of Job's fortunes, מ ׳רֵאשִׁיתְֱ Job 8:7 (opposed to מְאֹר יִשְׂגֶּה ); construct אֲנָשִׁים מִצְעַר 2Chr 24:24 a few men ; of time ׳לַמּ Isa 63:18 for the [ a ] little while. — Psa 42:7 see II. ׳מ .

occurrences.englishText: See now, this city is near to flee to, and it is a little one. Oh let me escape there (isn’t it a little one?), and my soul will live.”
See now, this city is near to flee to, and it is a little one. Oh let me escape there (isn’t it a little one?), and my soul will live.”

For the army of the Syrians came with a small company of men; and Yahweh delivered a very great army into their hand, because they had forsaken Yahweh, the God of their fathers. So they executed judgment on Joash.
Your holy people possessed it but a little while.
